posts.text: Strategic Energy Map is live: a free, ad-free map of global oil and gas infrastructure. Chokepoint ship traffic, facility status, pump prices and what-if scenarios, updated daily with every item sourced.
Diesel prices since the Strait of Hormuz closed: US +71%, EU average +40%, UK +38% (week of 21 Sep vs week of 23 Feb).

posts.text: 2 new developments today: Saudi Arabia's East-West pipeline has recovered to ~3.5 million b/d (about half capacity), and Kpler data show Hormuz crude exports averaging 7.4 million b/d in September (reported). Brent held near $105/bbl.

About 19.9 million b/d of oil crossed the Strait of Hormuz before the war. Pipelines around it had only ~3.5 million b/d of spare capacity (IEA, low estimate), leaving ~16.4 million b/d with no alternative route.
posts.alt: Bar chart, million barrels a day: oil through the Strait of Hormuz before the war 19.9; spare pipeline capacity around it 3.5; no alternative route 16.4.

posts.text: Saudi Arabia's Yanbu export terminal shows a 'major operational recovery' (Kpler satellite imagery), with Strait of Hormuz flows at a 13.2 million b/d 7-day average — about 77% of pre-war (reported). Brent $97/bbl, WTI $90/bbl as of 30 Sep.
Kpler and satellite imagery show a 'major operational recovery' at Saudi Arabia's Yanbu terminal. Strait of Hormuz flows are now a 13.2 million b/d 7-day average — about 77% of pre-war (reported).

Saudi Arabia's East-West pipeline runs ~1,200 km from Abqaiq to Yanbu, the kingdom's main Hormuz-bypass route. Shut by drone strikes on 11 Sep, it's back to about 3.5 million b/d — half its 7 million b/d capacity.

Before the 2026 crisis, about 23.2 million b/d of oil moved through the Strait of Malacca and 19.9 million b/d through Hormuz, each about a fifth of world demand. Suez, Bab el-Mandeb and the other chokepoints carried far less.
posts.alt: Bar chart of oil flows before the 2026 crisis, million barrels a day: Strait of Malacca 23.2, Strait of Hormuz 19.9, Suez Canal 4.9, Bab el-Mandeb 4.2, Turkish Straits 3.7, Panama Canal 2.3.

posts.text: JPMorgan and Goldman Sachs estimate Middle East crude flows are near pre-war levels, while UKMTO's delayed reports reveal 3 more Hormuz tanker attacks. Brent $99.74/bbl, WTI $91.45/bbl as of 1 Oct.

JPMorgan estimates Mideast crude shipments at 17.5 million b/d, 98% of pre-war, Hormuz near 13 million b/d. Goldman Sachs puts Gulf exports at 23.3 million b/d in September, matching 2025 — adapting to risk, not safer.

UKMTO disclosed 3 more Hormuz tanker attacks via delayed warnings, with vessel identities, damage and casualties still unconfirmed days later — a widening gap in incident reporting even as overall traffic recovers.

Aramco's Abqaiq plant stabilises up to 7 million b/d of crude, over half of Saudi output, before export on the East-West pipeline. Drones from Iraq hit it 27 Jul 2026; repair status isn't confirmed since.

AIS-tracked tanker traffic through Hormuz averaged 1.3/day in the week to 27 Sep, 97% below baseline — many sail dark, so broader tracking shows higher flows. Turkish Straits -48%, Bab el-Mandeb -22%.
posts.alt: Bar chart of 7-day average tanker transits vs pre-crisis baseline, percent change: Strait of Hormuz -97% (1.3/day), Turkish Straits -48% (11.7/day), Bab el-Mandeb -22% (9.4/day), Strait of Malacca -17% (70.0/day), Panama Canal -10% (11.7/day), Suez Canal -4% (15.0/day).
